source_text: Testimonium vero, ut ab auctore suo, ita etiam vel a probis, vel a improbis meretur, quod et illos iure provexerit, et istos iure damnaverit. Cum vero per se nec boni quidquam nec mali merentibus misericordiam liberalem esse permittit, nihil sentit iniuriae; quia et hoc ipsum, ut sit clemens operi suo Deus, cum in severitatem non cogitur, pars magna iustitiae est.
pass_a_gloss: But testimony it deserves, as from its author, so also either from the upright or from the wicked, because it has both advanced those by right and condemned these by right. But when it permits mercy to be liberal to those deserving through themselves neither anything of good nor of evil, it feels nothing of injury; because this itself also, that God be clement to his own work, when he is not driven into severity, is a great part of justice.

lemmas.lexica: LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: Justice deserves testimony not only from its author but also from good and wicked people alike: it has rightly exalted the former and rightly condemned the latter. When, however, it permits mercy to be generous to those who of themselves have earned neither good nor evil, it suffers no injury. For it is itself a great part of justice that God should be merciful to his own work when nothing compels him to severity.

choices.why: Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

choices.why: Keep Julian's good-of-nature vs good-of-will contrast; do not baptize as 'grace'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
